chunks: Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Let people not delude you from yourself, for verily recompense will reach you, not them. And let your day not be spent on this and that [trivialities], for indeed with you is one who records your deeds. And do not consider the little good [you do] to be insignificant, for indeed you will see it tomorrow in a way that will please you. And do not consider the little evil [you do] to be insignificant, for indeed you will see it tomorrow in a manner that will displease you. And do good, for I have not seen anything more intense in seeking out, nor quicker in catching up with, an old sin [and effacing it] than a good deed. Indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: Verily good deeds wipe out evil deeds. That is a reminder for the mindful.'
ai.seo_question: How do small good deeds affect old sins according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) advises ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb to focus on his own soul rather than being distracted by people, as individual recompense is personal. He encourages valuing small acts of good and evil, noting that good deeds swiftly erase old sins, citing the Quranic verse 11:114. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *takhfīf al-ḥisāb* (lightening of the reckoning) through consistent minor virtues, reflecting the practical spirituality found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 8.Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb who said, “

Abū ʿAbdillāh said to me, ‘Let people not delude you from yourself, for verily recompense [for your deeds] will reach you, not them. And let your day not be spent on this and that [which is of no benefit], for indeed with you is one who records your deeds. And do not consider the little good [you do] to be insignificant, for indeed you will see it tomorrow in a way that will please you. And do not consider the little evil [you do] to be insignificant, for indeed you will see it tomorrow in a manner that will displease you. And do good [to others], for I have not seen anything more intense in seeking out, nor quicker in catching up with, an old sin [and effacing it] than a good deed. Indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: Verily good deeds wipe out evil deeds. That is a reminder for the mindful. (Q11:114)”
